title: Playing the Apollo regularly 1939-50 and the theatre circuit
summary: Fields appeared at the Apollo nearly every year, where he gathered sidemen like Gene Ammons, Wallace Wilks and Bill Evans.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, how many times did you play the Apollo? Quite a number of times?
Oh, yes, quite a number of times. I would say that I doubt if I missed a single year between thirty nine and

fifty. I then came back again a little after fifty, but between thirty nine and fifty, it was rather regular, and one thing about it, that's one reason that so many names that I got acquainted with--because sometime I learned if I had a good nucleus I could be playing but didn't have to (inaudible). That's when Gene Ammons worked that circuit with me.

I got acquainted with those guys and I told them how many weeks I wanted them and we (inaudible). That's where I first got a hold of Wallace Wilks, the trumpet player, and I believe the first time Bill Evans was working with the band.

I was thinking just for that time and Bill said no, man; you see, that was good dough then but I told him, if you want to be in the band I can't guarantee you that kind of money and it turned out they
The theatres were better than the dances.
And they were very, very good contacts.
